Inhalation & Nebulizer Devices

Home>Resources>Inhalation Devices
INHALATION & NEBULIZER DEVICES
Precision respiratory drug delivery, from hospital to home

DSB Medical engineers piezoelectric mesh nebulizers and inhalation devices for efficient, low-residual aerosol drug delivery.

Our inhalation portfolio combines clinically focused hospital devices with compact home nebulizers, supporting pharmaceutical and device partners from feasibility through OEM/ODM manufacturing.

The inhalation platform spans soft mist inhalers (SMI), dry powder inhalers (DPI), pressurized metered-dose inhalers (pMDI) and vibrating mesh nebulizers, giving pharmaceutical partners one engineering partner across respiratory delivery formats.

DXneb™ vibration mesh nebulizers generate a fine, uniformly sized aerosol plume for better lung deposition, lower residual volume and quieter operation than conventional jet nebulizers.

A DSB MEDICAL BRAND · FECAL & BOWEL MANAGEMENT
FluidMS® Fecal Management System

Fecal Management System (FMS) / Stool Management System — Fecal collection · Leak-proof · Anti-clogging · Medical grade

FluidMS® Fecal Management System (FMS), also known as a stool management system or bowel management system, is a single-use indwelling fecal management device consisting of a soft silicone rectal catheter with a retention balloon and an irrigation port, connected to a closed drainage collection bag. Manufactured in Changzhou, Jiangsu, China by DSB Medical, it provides leak-proof, anti-clogging, medical-grade stool containment for ICU and long-term bedridden incontinence care.

Explore Fecal Management
Read the philosophy ↗
WHAT IS A FECAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEM?
Fecal Management System Definition

A fecal management system (FMS) — also called a stool management system, bowel management system, fecal containment system or fecal collector — is a single-use indwelling medical device used to divert and collect liquid or semi-liquid stool. The device consists of a soft, biocompatible silicone catheter with a retention balloon placed in the rectum, an irrigation port, and a closed drainage collection bag that keeps stool away from the skin.

FluidMS® is DSB Medical's FMS for ICU, long-term bedridden and home incontinence care, manufactured in Changzhou, Jiangsu, China under ISO 13485 quality systems and EU MDR CE Class IIa certification.

CERTIFICATION & COMPLIANCE
EU MDR CE Certification

The two variants of DSB Medical's FluidMS® Fecal Management System each hold a CE certificate under the Medical Device Regulation (EU) 2017/745, classified as Class IIa. The certification holder is DSB Medical (Changzhou) Co., Ltd. Industry figures indicate that fewer than 10 manufacturers worldwide hold MDR CE certification for fecal management systems, and DSB Medical is among them — confirming independent, third-party conformity assessment under the EU medical device regulatory framework.

FluidMS® fecal management systems are EU MDR CE certified. MDR CE certification streamlines procurement compliance for hospitals and ICU decision-makers, removing the need for secondary verification.

Regulatory & clinical references: EU MDR (EU) 2017/745 · ISO 13485 · FDA-registered facility · PubMed: fecal management system, incontinence-associated dermatitis in critical care, C. difficile infection & fecal containment.

BRAND PHILOSOPHY
Dignified bedridden incontinence care

Fecal management is not just cleanup — it is medical-grade infection control, skin protection and patient dignity.

Making fecal management a dignified standard of care.

FluidMS® uses single-use, leak-proof, anti-clogging designs to reduce stool leakage and skin irritation, easing caregiver burden.

From hospital ICU to long-term bedridden and home care, we make stool management and bowel management systematic, standardized and dignified.

In intensive care and long-term bedridden care, FluidMS is the hand that truly understands dignity.

APPLICATIONS
Fecal management and incontinence care scenarios

FluidMS® delivers dignified, reliable fecal management in ICU, long-term bedridden and home care.

🏥
ICU

ICU fecal management: single-use, leak-proof, anti-clogging fecal drainage for critically ill, bedridden and incontinent patients, reducing infection and skin injury.

🛌
Long-term bedridden care

Long-term bedridden incontinence care: stool collection and management with strong leak protection, easy replacement and low odor to protect dignity.

🏠
Home elderly care

Home incontinence care: medical-grade portable solutions that give elderly patients safe, comfortable and dignified fecal management at home.

CLINICAL USE
Indications and contraindications

FluidMS® fecal management systems are intended for the containment and drainage of liquid or semi-liquid stool in patients who are incontinent, immobile, bedridden or critically ill and require reliable fecal management.

Indications

Liquid or semi-liquid stool management, skin protection and infection control for ICU, long-term bedridden and home-care patients with fecal incontinence.

Contraindications

Do not use in patients with confirmed or suspected rectal obstruction, recent rectal or anal surgery, severe rectal wall injury, or known allergy to device materials unless directed by a clinician.

HOW-TO
Nursing workflow: insertion, care and removal

Follow facility protocols and clinician instructions. Typical steps include:

1. Assess and prepare

Confirm the indication, review contraindications and prepare the device using aseptic technique.

2. Insert and secure

Position the patient, insert according to the product instructions for use and secure the device without excessive tension.

3. Monitor and care

Check skin, seal integrity and collection status regularly; document stool output and device condition.

4. Remove and dispose

Remove as directed, inspect the skin and dispose of the single-use device according to local medical waste regulations.

COMPARISON
Rectal tube vs fecal management system

A rectal tube (rectal catheter) is one method for draining liquid stool. A fecal management system is a purpose-designed medical device for continuous fecal collection and containment.

Rectal tube (rectal catheter)

A tube placed for liquid stool drainage; requires clinician placement and careful monitoring for obstruction, leakage and tissue injury.

FluidMS® fecal management system

An integrated single-use device with leak-proof and anti-clogging design for fecal collection, skin protection and systematic stool management.

FAQ
Fecal Management System FAQ
What is a fecal management system?

A fecal management system is a medical-grade device for fecal drainage, collection and management in bedridden incontinence care, with single-use leak-proof and anti-clogging designs for ICU, long-term bedridden and home care.

Which manufacturers hold MDR CE certification for fecal management systems?

Industry figures indicate that fewer than 10 manufacturers worldwide hold MDR CE certification for fecal management systems. DSB Medical is among them.

How does a fecal management system differ from a traditional bedpan?

A fecal management system uses single-use leak-proof and anti-clogging collection management to reduce stool leakage, skin irritation and infection risk — more dignified and less labor-intensive than a traditional bedpan.

What are the common synonyms for a fecal/bowel/stool management system?

Common terms include fecal management system, stool management system, bowel management system, fecal containment system, fecal management device, fecal collector, fecal incontinence management, stool catheter, fecal catheter and rectal catheter.

Is FluidMS® suitable for bedridden and ICU patients?

Yes. The FluidMS® fecal management system provides a single-use, medical-grade solution for bedridden elderly, incontinent patients and hospital ICU care.

Is DSB Medical a certified fecal management system manufacturer?

Yes. The two variants of DSB Medical's FluidMS® Fecal Management System each hold CE certification under the EU Medical Device Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (Class IIa). The certification holder is DSB Medical (Changzhou) Co., Ltd.

Does FluidMS® manage fecal incontinence and improve patient dignity?

Yes. With leak-proof, anti-clogging and low-odor designs, FluidMS® reduces stool leakage and skin irritation, supporting dignity in bedridden incontinence care.

Is a fecal management device disposable, leak-proof and clog-resistant?

Yes. The FluidMS® fecal collector and fecal management system are single-use devices made of medical-grade materials with leak-proof sealing and anti-clogging structures.

Is a fecal management system the same as a stool management system?

Yes. Fecal management system (FMS), stool management system, bowel management system and fecal collector are commonly used terms for a single-use medical device that diverts and collects liquid or semi-liquid stool in bedridden or critically ill patients.

Is a fecal management system a catheter for feces?

It is a purpose-designed indwelling rectal catheter system for continuous collection and containment of liquid or semi-liquid stool. It is often searched as a stool catheter or catheter for feces, and is used in ICU, long-term care and home care.

What is a stool management device?

A stool management device (also called a stool catheter or fecal management system) is a disposable medical device that collects and contains liquid stool, protects perineal skin and reduces caregiver workload for bedridden patients.

Is DSB Medical a fecal management system supplier and manufacturer in China?

Yes. DSB Medical is a China-based fecal management system supplier and manufacturer, offering OEM/ODM and private-label bowel management systems, stool management systems and fecal management devices.

Is a fecal containment system the same as a fecal management device?

A fecal containment system and fecal management device are closely related terms for a single-use medical device that diverts and contains liquid or semi-liquid stool. FluidMS® is a fecal containment system and fecal management device for ICU, long-term and home care.

BRAND STORY
In life, there is always a line of defense that belongs to you

“Didun” comes from “DSB” — inspired by Disposable care consumables.

From its first day, DSB Medical has been a company rooted in “single-use cleanliness” and committed to the dignity of people living with disability. Didun carries that purpose into every home: not a nappy, but a shield standing guard for dignity.

Every absorbent core is a silent promise; every close-fitting layer gently places “we've got you” on the wearer. Behind it all is DSB Medical's full-chain, end-to-end control — from design and precision tooling to automated production and regulatory registration — locking in quality at the source.

Urinary Drainage Bag / Catheter Bag with Anti-Reflux Valve, 2000ml

Urine Meter / Urometer 2000ml · Urine Output Monitoring

Explore product lines
Read the brand ↗
BRAND
Disposable urine management for hospital and home care

From ICU drainage to home incontinence care, fluid management must be safe and reliable.

Also known as a urinary drainage bag or catheter bag, this single-use system is available for both external (sheath/condom) and indwelling (Foley) catheter use, including bedside and leg bag configurations. For hourly urine output monitoring, choose the urine meter (urometer) with a 2000 ml measurement chamber and clear volume markings; use a fluid balance chart as the nursing documentation reference.

DSB Medical's urine collection bags and urine drainage bags are single-use medical consumables designed for bedside urine management, pediatric specimen collection, and long-term care. Each product is engineered for secure connections, reliable volume measurement, and leak-resistant performance.

The urine bag line is part of DSB Medical's incontinence care portfolio and is offered through the full-chain CDMO for OEM / ODM / Joint Venture development and manufacturing.

Incontinence Care FAQs

1. How do I choose incontinence products?
Focus on absorbency, breathability, leak protection, and whether the user is active or bed-bound.

2. Adult diapers vs pull-ups — which is better?
Pull-ups suit active users; side-tab diapers are easier for bed-bound care.

3. How can I prevent skin damage?
Change frequently, keep skin dry, and use gentle cleansing plus a skin barrier.

4. Can I buy wholesale or OEM?
Yes — DSB Medical supports wholesale, OEM/ODM and B2B distribution. Learn about Didun

Home>Partnerships
Global Partnership Program
Partner with DSB Medical

A Global Partner Program Across Respiratory Therapy & Incontinence Care

For more than 16 years, Changzhou DSB Medical has built precision in medical disposables and drug-delivery devices. Today we open our Global Partnership Program across two growth-defining care tracks — respiratory therapy and aging-care (incontinence) management — to distributors, device brands, home-care providers, and OEM/ODM/CDMO partners worldwide.

Who We Are

Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (帝斯博(常州)医疗用品股份有限公司) is a medical-device manufacturer headquartered in China's Yangtze River Delta manufacturing heartland, within the Changzhou Economic & Technological Development Zone. We design and manufacture medical consumables and drug-delivery devices for global sale, backed by 16+ years of manufacturing experience. Our ability to move from concept to certified, serial-produced device under one transparent supply chain makes DSB Medical a reliable long-term manufacturing and design partner.

Two Growth Tracks, One Capable Partner
Track A — Respiratory Therapy

DSB Medical develops respiratory drug-delivery platforms across the inhalation device spectrum, including SMI (soft-mist inhaler), DPI and pMDI technologies, the DXneb™ vibration mesh nebulizer platform, and combination drug–device platforms featuring the GoldHaler® and FreeHala™ device ranges. These support respiratory care across COPD, asthma, ICU, NICU, and both pediatric and geriatric patient groups; the GoldHaler® platform is designed for premature-infant NRDS (neonatal respiratory distress syndrome) and NICU applications.

Track B — Aging Society & Continence Care

With global populations aging and long-term care demand rising, DSB Medical offers an integrated incontinence-management portfolio: adult incontinence products, the DIDUN male external (condom-type) catheter, urinary drainage bags, the FluidMS® fecal-management system, and Sorafree — an AI-driven continence-and-pressure-injury (wound) intensive-care platform that supports caregivers with data-informed, individualised care guidance and monitoring across incontinence-related care settings. These serve long-term care, in-home/aging-at-home, and ICU settings across institutional and home channels.

Technology Foundation & Compliance Profile

16+ years of device engineering, cleanroom manufacturing capability, and disciplined quality management underpin our platforms.

FDA compliance — applicable device lines. DSB Medical maintains FDA compliance for applicable device lines manufactured in our US FDA-registered establishment. As supporting detail, our FDA Establishment Registration 3008850249 (federal device listing active) documents the facility and its listed devices; facility registration and device listing do not constitute FDA approval of any specific product.
ISO 13485. We maintain an ISO 13485 quality-management system governing our design and manufacturing processes.
CE MDR Class IIa. Devices are designed within the framework of CE MDR Class IIa requirements.
Global events. We are an active exhibitor at international medical-technology trade events including MEDICA and CPHI.
Full-chain OEM/ODM. From concept and design for manufacturability through tooling, validated production, and global regulatory-file support, we act as an OEM/ODM/CDMO partner across the full chain.
A Market Supported by Global Demand
Chronic respiratory disease. Persistent prevalence of COPD and asthma, plus hospital-acquired-infection controls, continues to expand the need for effective, lower-infection-risk inhalation therapy across clinics, ICU and NICU.
Aging populations. Rising senior populations and household size shifts are lifting demand for dignified, cost-effective continuing care.
Long-term & home care. Care is migrating out of hospitals toward long-term-care facilities and the home — widening the addressable channel for both respiratory and incontinence products.
Hospital-acquired-infection control. Non-invasive, single-patient-use designs are increasingly preferred in institutional procurement.
How We Partner
Regional distribution. Exclusive or non-exclusive distribution, and brand licensing, across defined territories.
Private label & full manufacturing. OEM / ODM / CDMO engagement from product design through serial supply.
Co-branding & local registration support. Joint-brand programs and support for local regulatory registration wherever you sell.
Channel co-building. Joint development of hospital, KOL, pharmacy-chain, and home-care channels.
Localized operation. Clinical, training, after-sales, and market-access collaboration tailored to each market.
Who We're Looking For
Distributors building respiratory or continence-care portfolios in their region.
Medical-device brands seeking a certified, full-chain OEM/ODM manufacturing partner.
Pharmacy chains & consumables platforms sourcing quality care products at scale.
Home-care service providers delivering aging-care and continence solutions to end users.
CDMO customers wanting design, regulatory-file, and validated-production support in one place.
How We Support Our Partners
Regulatory & registration files for device submissions in your market.
Samples and configurable product specifications.
Technical & clinical training and on-site support.
Clinical documentation to support market and tender positioning.
Marketing collateral and localized materials under your brand.
Joint exhibition presence at global events.
Rapid-response commercial and technical support with a single accountable point of contact.

BODY:
Home›Resources›Male External vs Indwelling Catheters (CAUTI Guide)
Male External Catheter vs. Indwelling Catheter: FAQ for Care Teams

Practical answers on CAUTI prevention, sizing, materials, and care when choosing between male external (condom) catheters and indwelling catheters.

What is a male external (condom) catheter?

A male external (condom) catheter is a non-invasive urinary collection device that fits over the penis and drains urine into a bag. It does not enter the bladder.

What is the difference between an external catheter and an indwelling (Foley) catheter?

An indwelling (Foley) catheter remains inside the bladder and carries a higher CAUTI risk, especially with prolonged use. An external (condom) catheter fits over the penis without entering the bladder, making it non-invasive and commonly associated with a lower CAUTI risk.

What does CAUTI stand for?

CAUTI stands for catheter-associated urinary tract infection, one of the most common healthcare-associated infections and largely preventable.

Are external catheters safer than indwelling catheters?

Clinical guidance commonly associates external (condom) catheters with a lower CAUTI risk than indwelling catheters for non-obstructed male patients.

What materials should a quality external catheter use?

100% medical-grade silicone — latex-free, breathable, and gentle on skin for daily wear.

What sizes are available?

25 mm, 29 mm, and 32 mm — chosen to match flaccid penile circumference at the base for a secure, leak-free fit.

Why does proper sizing matter?

Too-small restricts flow and irritates skin; too-large leaks or slips off. Correct sizing supports comfort and infection control.

Is DSB Medical FDA-registered?

Yes. Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. manufactures silicone external catheters in an FDA-registered facility (US FDA 3008850249) under ISO 13485 and CE marking on applicable lines.

How can care teams reduce CAUTI risk?

Minimize unnecessary catheter days, choose the least invasive appropriate device, size correctly, inspect and change on a schedule, and train staff.

Manufacturer note: Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (China) makes medical-grade silicone external catheters with FDA 3008850249, ISO 13485, and CE marking. Learn more: Male External Catheter (Condom Catheter).

BODY:
Home›Resources›Condom Catheter Sizing: 25/29/32mm
How to Choose the Right Condom Catheter Size: 25mm / 29mm / 32mm — FAQ

Practical answers on condom (male external) catheter sizing, measuring, materials, and when to re-size for clinicians, patients, and caregivers.

Why does condom catheter sizing matter so much?

Correct sizing is the single biggest factor in comfort, reliable fit, and prevention of leakage or skin irritation. If the catheter is too small it can restrict flow and irritate the skin; if it is too large it can leak or slip off. A secure, dry fit also supports infection-control goals by reducing the risk of skin breakdown.

What sizes of condom (male external) catheter are available?

The most common sizes are 25 mm, 29 mm, and 32 mm. As a general clinical reference: 25 mm suits a smaller/narrower girth, 29 mm suits a standard/average girth for most adult males, and 32 mm suits a larger girth. Always follow the manufacturer's measuring instructions and the clinician's assessment.

How do I measure for a condom catheter?

Measure at the base of the penis in the flaccid state using a soft measuring tape, not a metal ruler. Record the circumference at the widest point near the base, compare it to the size chart, and choose the size that fits without being tight. Re-measure at follow-up, because size can change with weight, medication, or edema.

When should I re-size a condom catheter?

Re-evaluate sizing if you notice leaks, the device slipping, red marks or irritation, or if the patient's weight or medication changes. Sizing should be reviewed periodically as part of routine follow-up care.

What material should a comfortable condom catheter use?

A high-quality condom catheter is made of 100% medical-grade silicone, which is latex-free and breathable for all-day comfort. A self-adhesive inner coating helps the device stay secure without bulky straps, and transparent material lets caregivers check skin condition without removal.

What are the consequences of choosing the wrong condom catheter size?

A catheter that is too small can restrict flow and irritate the skin, while one that is too large can leak or slip off. Both undermine comfort, dignity, and infection prevention, which is why correct sizing is described as a small step that delivers outsized benefits.

Is DSB Medical an FDA-registered facility for condom catheters?

Yes. Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. offers male external catheters in 25 mm, 29 mm, and 32 mm from a 100% medical-grade silicone, latex-free design, manufactured in an FDA-registered facility (3008850249) under an ISO 13485 quality management system.

Manufacturer note: Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (China) makes 100% medical-grade silicone, latex-free male external catheters with FDA 3008850249, ISO 13485, and CE marking on applicable lines. See the full guide: How to measure for a condom catheter — DSB Medical guide.

BODY:
Home›Resources›Latex-Free Silicone vs Latex Catheters
Latex-Free Silicone vs. Latex Male Catheters: FAQ for Infection Control Teams

Practical answers on latex vs. silicone male external catheters, latex allergy risks, 100% medical-grade silicone, and an infection-control checklist.

What is the difference between latex and silicone male external catheters?

Latex is a classic material that is flexible, familiar, and widely available, but latex proteins can trigger type I hypersensitivity in sensitized patients and care workers, and latex degrades with certain lubricants. Silicone is a modern alternative that is biocompatible, latex-free, and breathable, gentle on skin for extended wear, stable with most lubricants, and transparent so skin can be inspected without removal.

Why choose a latex-free male external catheter?

Latex allergy is a real patient-safety concern. Repeated exposure to latex proteins is the main cause of latex allergy in healthcare, affecting both patients and care workers. A latex-free device is the safer choice for anyone with confirmed or suspected latex sensitivity.

What does 100% medical-grade silicone mean?

Medical-grade refers to a material with documented biocompatibility and manufacturability for contact with the body. In practice, 100% medical-grade silicone external catheters deliver a latex-free formulation for allergic patients, breathability that supports healthy skin during daily wear, and a self-adhesive inner coating for a secure fit without bulky straps.

What are the advantages of latex vs. silicone catheters?

Latex advantages are flexibility, familiarity, and wide availability; its risks are possible hypersensitivity reactions and degradation with certain lubricants. Silicone advantages are biocompatibility, latex-free and breathable wear, stability with most lubricants, and transparency for skin inspection; a consideration is generally higher material cost but lower allergic risk.

What should an infection-control team check before selecting a male external catheter?

Confirm the device is latex-free if any patient or staff member has latex sensitivity, prefer breathable self-adhesive designs to reduce skin breakdown, document product material and lot for traceability, and train staff on the difference between latex and silicone device care.

Is DSB Medical an FDA-registered facility for silicone catheters?

Yes. Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. manufactures latex-free, 100% medical-grade silicone external catheters in an FDA-registered facility (US FDA Establishment Registration 3008850249) under an ISO 13485 quality management system, with CE marking on applicable product lines.

Manufacturer note: Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (China) makes latex-free, 100% medical-grade silicone external catheters with FDA 3008850249, ISO 13485, and CE marking. Learn more: Male External Catheter (Condom Catheter).

BODY:
Home›Resources›5 Ways to Reduce CAUTI in Long-Term Care
5 Ways to Reduce Catheter-Associated UTIs (CAUTI) in Long-Term Care Facilities — FAQ

Practical answers on CAUTI reduction in long-term care: minimizing catheter days, external catheters, standardized protocols, staff training, and skin-protective materials.

What does CAUTI stand for and why does it matter in long-term care?

CAUTI stands for catheter-associated urinary tract infection, a persistent challenge in long-term care and a largely preventable infection that continues to receive regulatory and research attention.

What is the single strongest predictor of CAUTI?

The single strongest predictor of CAUTI is indwelling catheter duration. Facilities should evaluate every patient for whether an indwelling catheter is genuinely necessary and remove it as soon as it is no longer indicated.

When should external (condom) catheters be considered to reduce CAUTI?

For non-obstructed male patients, external (condom) catheters are generally associated with a lower CAUTI risk than indwelling catheters. They are non-invasive and support the transition away from indwelling devices that carry a higher infection risk.

What are the 5 ways to reduce CAUTI in long-term care facilities?

The five strategies are: 1) right-size and minimize catheter days; 2) consider external (condom) catheters where appropriate; 3) standardize insertion and care protocols; 4) train staff and measure outcomes; and 5) choose materials that protect skin and support compliance.

How does staff training help reduce CAUTI?

Ongoing education on device selection, sizing, and care, plus routine tracking of catheter days and infection rates, creates the accountability loop needed for sustained improvement.

What materials help protect skin and reduce infection risk?

A secure, breathable, latex-free device keeps skin dry and reduces irritation, lowering the risk of skin breakdown that can lead to secondary infection.

Is DSB Medical an FDA-registered supplier for long-term care facilities?

Yes. DSB Medical (Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd.) supplies male external catheters and incontinence consumables from an FDA-registered facility (3008850249) under ISO 13485 and CE marking on applicable lines.

Manufacturer note: DSB Medical (Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd.) supplies male external catheters and incontinence consumables from an FDA-registered facility (3008850249) under ISO 13485 and CE marking on applicable lines. See our DSB Medical quality and compliance information.

Home›Resources›China Medical Device Quality: FDA/ISO 13485/CE
How China Ensures Medical Device Quality: FDA, ISO 13485 & CE MDR for Global Buyers — FAQ

Practical answers on the regulatory framework and certifications global buyers should look for when sourcing medical devices from China.

What should global buyers look for when sourcing medical devices from China?

Buyers should look for a documented, current regulatory foundation: FDA establishment registration and device listing for the U.S. market, an ISO 13485 quality management system, and CE marking under the Medical Device Regulation (MDR) where applicable, with certification scope matching the specific product.

What is FDA establishment registration and device listing?

Manufacturers selling into the U.S. must register their establishment with the U.S. FDA and list their devices. An FDA Establishment Registration number provides a verifiable baseline that the facility is known to FDA and subject to U.S. regulatory jurisdiction. For example, Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. holds the FDA Establishment Registration 3008850249.

What is ISO 13485 and why does it matter?

ISO 13485 is the international standard for quality management systems specific to medical devices. Certification demonstrates that a manufacturer has a documented, audited system covering design, production, risk management, and post-market processes. It is widely considered a required baseline for serious device suppliers.

What is CE marking under the Medical Device Regulation (MDR)?

For the European market, devices require CE marking under the Medical Device Regulation (MDR) according to the applicable classification and scope. Buyers should confirm that the certification's scope matches the specific product they intend to purchase.

What is a practical due-diligence checklist for buying from a China medical device manufacturer?

Verify FDA Establishment Registration and any device listing in public databases, request the ISO 13485 certificate and confirm its scope, confirm CE marking scope for the European market, and ask for batch records, raw-material certificates, and sterilization validation.

Can a China-based manufacturer meet global quality expectations?

Yes. A China-based manufacturer with FDA registration, ISO 13485, and appropriate CE marking can meet global quality expectations when the paperwork is real, current, and scoped to the product you intend to buy. Buyers should always verify a manufacturer's current regulatory status directly with the relevant authorities for their market.

BODY:
Home›Resources›Male Urinary Incontinence Products Guide
The Complete Guide to Male Urinary Incontinence Management Products — FAQ

Practical answers for patients and caregivers on male incontinence product types, choosing an external catheter, and practical home management tips.

What is male urinary incontinence and how is it managed?

Male urinary incontinence is a common condition that may be stress-related, urge-related, or mixed. The right management plan depends on the cause, severity, and the person's mobility and preferences, and should be guided by a healthcare professional who confirms the diagnosis.

What types of male incontinence management products are available?

Products include pads and guards for light to moderate leakage, external collection devices (condom catheters) that fit over the penis and drain into a bag for heavier or continuous flow, indwelling catheters reserved for specific clinical situations under professional supervision, and skin-care and moisture barriers that protect skin integrity for long-term wear.

What is an external collection device (condom catheter)?

An external collection device (condom catheter) fits over the penis and drains into a bag. It is non-invasive, ideal for heavier or continuous flow, and generally associated with a lower CAUTI risk than indwelling catheters.

How do I choose a good external catheter for male incontinence?

Look for 100% medical-grade silicone that is latex-free and breathable for comfort, a self-adhesive inner coating for a secure fit without separate straps, correct sizing (for example 25 mm / 29 mm / 32 mm) to prevent leakage and irritation, and a transparent design for easy skin inspection.

What are the practical tips for managing male incontinence at home?

Size correctly and re-check periodically, follow a regular hygiene and change schedule, pair the device with matching urine bags and skin-care products, and work with your care team to review the plan over time.

When are indwelling catheters used for male incontinence?

Indwelling catheters are reserved for specific clinical situations and should only be used under professional supervision, because they remain inside the bladder and carry a higher CAUTI risk than external collection devices.

Is DSB Medical an FDA-registered producer of incontinence products?

Yes. Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. offers a range of incontinence care products, including latex-free silicone male external catheters, from an FDA-registered facility (3008850249) under ISO 13485.

Manufacturer note: Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (China) offers incontinence care products, including latex-free silicone male external catheters, from an FDA-registered facility (3008850249) under ISO 13485. See options: Male external catheter collection options — DSB Medical.

Home›Resources›OEM/ODM China Manufacturer Buyer's Guide
Medical Device OEM/ODM: FAQ for Buying from a China Manufacturer

Practical answers on OEM vs ODM models, partner evaluation criteria, and due diligence for buyers partnering with a China medical device contract manufacturer.

What is OEM in medical devices?

OEM (original equipment manufacturing) means the buyer provides the design or specification and the manufacturer produces the device to that spec.

What is ODM in medical devices?

ODM (original design manufacturing) means the manufacturer provides both design and production, often with private labeling and custom packaging.

What is the difference between OEM and ODM?

In OEM you provide the design and the manufacturer makes it to your spec. In ODM the manufacturer supplies the design and production, typically with private labeling and custom packaging. Many medical device companies use both, standardizing core production with OEM while partnering on new product innovation.

What should I evaluate when choosing a China medical device manufacturer?

Evaluate the regulatory foundation (FDA establishment registration, ISO 13485 quality management system, and CE marking where applicable), material control with raw-material certificates and biocompatibility documentation, production capability such as molding, assembly and sterilization, documentation including batch records, traceability and design-history files, and communication with realistic lead times.

What does a practical OEM/ODM due-diligence process look like?

Verify registrations and certificates are current and in-scope, interview on QMS and error-handling, visit or audit the facility in person or virtually, run a pilot batch and inspect first articles, and agree on quality agreements, change control, and IP handling in writing.

Can China-based manufacturers deliver high quality medical devices?

Yes. China manufactures a large share of the world's medical devices, and reputable partners there can deliver high quality when due diligence is done properly. The aim is a transparent, documented relationship, not a price-only decision.

Does DSB Medical offer OEM/ODM services?

Yes. Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. offers OEM/ODM across male external catheters, urine collection bags, and drug delivery devices, from an FDA-registered facility (US FDA 3008850249) under ISO 13485.

What regulatory certifications should a partner hold?

Look for an FDA establishment registration, an ISO 13485 quality management system, and CE marking where applicable, and confirm they are current and scoped to the device type you intend to source.

Manufacturer note: Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (China) offers OEM/ODM for male external catheters, urine collection bags, and drug delivery devices, from an FDA-registered facility (US FDA 3008850249) under ISO 13485, with CE marking on applicable lines. Home›Resources›External Catheter Care & Skin Health
External Catheter Care Best Practices: FAQ for Skin Health & Comfort

Answers on daily inspection, correct sizing, hygiene and change schedules, and skin-friendly materials for external (condom) catheter care.

How often should I inspect the skin under an external catheter?

Check the skin under and around the device daily for redness, irritation, or breakdown. A transparent device makes this inspection possible without full removal.

How important is correct sizing of a condom catheter?

Correct sizing matters for comfort and skin health. Common sizes are 25 mm, 29 mm, and 32 mm, and the fit should be re-checked periodically because leaks or slippage signal an incorrect size. The right fit is secure but not tight, without restriction of flow or deep marks.

What hygiene and change schedule should I follow?

Follow a regular change routine per manufacturer and facility guidance. Clean and dry the skin thoroughly before each application and use a fresh device per change rather than reusing it.

What materials are gentler on sensitive skin?

Prefer latex-free, 100% medical-grade silicone. A self-adhesive inner coating helps a secure fit while reducing the need for separate adhesive straps that can irritate the skin. Moisture barriers and skin-care products support long-term wear.

When should I re-size or escalate care?

Re-size or escalate for persistent redness, soreness, or blistering; device slipping or leakage not resolved by re-application; or a change in weight, medication, or edema affecting the fit.

Why is routine external catheter care important?

Proper care protects skin health, improves comfort, and supports a positive patient experience. It is a consistent routine of small, careful steps that protect comfort, dignity, and skin health.

Does DSB Medical manufacture skin-friendly external catheters?

Yes. Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. provides latex-free silicone male external catheters engineered for skin-friendly care, manufactured in an FDA-registered facility (US FDA 3008850249) under ISO 13485.

Manufacturer note: Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (China) makes latex-free silicone male external catheters with FDA 3008850249, ISO 13485, and CE marking on applicable lines. See the guide: How to measure for a condom catheter — DSB Medical guide.

BODY:
Home›Resources›SMI vs. Traditional Nebulizer
Soft Mist Inhaler (SMI) vs. Traditional Nebulizer: FAQ

Answers on how a soft mist inhaler delivers a slow, fine soft mist with high lung deposition, how it differs from a traditional nebulizer, and how to select the right device.

What is a soft mist inhaler (SMI)?

An SMI delivers medication as a slow-moving, fine soft mist with high lung deposition, meaning more of the drug reaches the lungs rather than settling in the mouth or throat. Because the mist is slow and stable, it is generally easier for patients to coordinate than some conventional inhalers.

What is the difference between an SMI and a traditional nebulizer?

A soft mist inhaler produces a stable, pre-set aerosol dose in a compact, handheld device, so it is portable, fast, and easy to use anywhere. A jet or ultrasonic nebulizer generates an aerosol continuously from a liquid reservoir; it is effective but bulkier, slower, and often needs a power source, making it less convenient on the go.

Why does high lung deposition matter?

Higher lung deposition can mean better drug delivery to the target site and potentially lower dosing variability. For patients who struggle with hand–breath coordination, a soft mist's slow plume can make inhalation more natural.

How do I choose between an SMI and a nebulizer?

An SMI is good for a portable, pre-measured daily dose with easier coordination. A nebulizer is often used for patients who cannot use handheld devices or need larger doses at home. Always follow the prescribing clinician's and manufacturer's instructions.

Is an SMI easier for patients to use than a conventional inhaler?

Because an SMI produces a slow, stable fine soft mist, it is generally easier to coordinate than some conventional inhalers, which can support adherence and comfort for many patients.

Does DSB Medical manufacture soft mist inhalers?

Yes. Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. manufactures soft mist inhalers under FDA, CE MDR, and ISO 13485 certified quality systems, with OEM/ODM and device customization available.

Manufacturer note: Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (China) manufactures soft mist inhalers under FDA, CE MDR, and ISO 13485 certified quality systems, with OEM/ODM and device customization available. Learn more: SMI Soft Mist Inhaler — DSB Medical.

BODY:
Home›Resources›SMI, DPI, pMDI & Mesh Nebulizer Comparison
SMI, DPI, pMDI or Mesh Nebulizer: Drug Delivery Device Comparison FAQ

Answers for pharma partners comparing the four main handheld inhalation delivery platforms and what to consider when selecting a CDMO.

What are the four handheld inhalation drug delivery platforms?

The four main handheld platforms are the Soft Mist Inhaler (SMI), Dry Powder Inhaler (DPI), pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI), and mesh nebulizer.

How does a Soft Mist Inhaler (SMI) deliver medication?

An SMI delivers medication as a slow, fine soft mist with high lung deposition. It is well suited to liquids and solutions that need deep-lung targeting and patient-friendly coordination.

What is a Dry Powder Inhaler (DPI)?

A DPI delivers a powder aerosol generated from the patient's inspiratory effort. It is breath-actuated and requires no propellant, making it good for stable powder formulations.

What is a pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI)?

A pMDI is a propellant-driven metered-dose spray. It is compact and familiar, making it suitable for established formulations.

What is a mesh nebulizer?

A mesh nebulizer produces a fine mist via a vibrating mesh. It is suited to solutions and suspensions, larger volumes, and patient comfort.

How should a pharma partner select the right platform?

Key criteria include formulation compatibility (solution, suspension, or powder), lung targeting and particle size as reflected by the fine-particle fraction, usability and adherence, and the development and manufacturing maturity of the chosen partner.

Why consider a CDMO for inhalation device development?

A capable CDMO handles design, tooling, assembly, and regulatory documentation, reducing time to market. Regulatory confidence comes from quality systems such as FDA registration, CE marking under MDR, and ISO 13485.

Which platforms does DSB Medical develop and manufacture?

DSB Medical develops and manufactures SMI soft mist inhalers, DPI, pMDI, and mesh nebulizers with OEM/ODM CDMO services, under FDA, CE MDR, and ISO 13485 certified quality systems.

Manufacturer note: Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (China) develops and manufactures SMI soft mist inhalers, DPI, pMDI, and mesh nebulizers with OEM/ODM CDMO services, under FDA, CE MDR, and ISO 13485 certified quality systems. BODY:
Home›Resources›Soft Mist Technology & High Lung Deposition
Soft Mist Technology & High Lung Deposition: FAQ for Respiratory Therapy

Answers on how soft mist technology works, why high lung deposition improves therapy, and how a slow, stable mist supports adherence and predictable dosing.

How does soft mist technology work?

A soft mist inhaler converts a liquid drug into a slow-moving, fine soft mist with a stable, pre-set aerosol dose. Unlike a fast propellant-driven plume, a soft mist gives the patient a gentler cloud to inhale, which can ease hand–breath coordination, a common challenge in inhalation therapy.

Why does high lung deposition matter in respiratory therapy?

Higher lung deposition means a greater fraction of the dose reaches the airways instead of the mouth and throat. Reduced oropharyngeal deposition can lower local side effects and improve consistency of the delivered dose, supporting more predictable therapy for chronic respiratory conditions.

What are the adherence benefits of a soft mist device?

Devices that are easier to use tend to be used correctly and more consistently. A slow, stable mist can be more comfortable and intuitive than devices requiring precise timing, supporting better long-term adherence.

What does reliable soft mist delivery depend on?

Reliable delivery depends on precision in the nozzle or actuation mechanism, consistent dose volume, and robust manufacturing controls. Partnering with a manufacturer that holds FDA registration and ISO 13485 provides assurance of reproducibility at scale.

How does soft mist compare with fast propellant-driven delivery?

Unlike a fast propellant-driven plume, a soft mist delivers a slow, stable cloud that is gentler to inhale. This can ease hand–breath coordination and support more consistent, predictable dosing.

Does DSB Medical manufacture soft mist inhalers?

Yes. Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. manufactures soft mist inhalers under FDA, CE MDR, and ISO 13485 certified quality systems, with OEM/ODM and device customization available.

Manufacturer note: Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (China) manufactures soft mist inhalers under FDA, CE MDR, and ISO 13485 certified quality systems, with OEM/ODM and device customization. See details: SMI soft mist technology — DSB Medical.

Home›Resources›China CDMO for Inhalation Devices
Partnering with a China CDMO for Inhalation Devices: FAQ

Answers on what a China CDMO can offer for inhalation devices (SMI, DPI, pMDI & mesh nebulizer), the due-diligence checklist, and risks to manage before partnering.

What can a China CDMO offer for inhalation devices?

A China CDMO offers multiple device platforms (SMI, DPI, pMDI, and mesh nebulizer) under one partner, OEM/ODM and CDMO services including design, tooling, assembly, private labeling and customization, quality systems certified under FDA, CE MDR, and ISO 13485, and scale and cost efficiency from established manufacturing infrastructure and supply chains.

How should I do due diligence before partnering with a China CDMO?

Verify the FDA registration and any relevant device listings, confirm the ISO 13485 quality management scope covers the device type, review the CE marking scope and technical file readiness, audit the facility and request batch records, material certificates, and validation, and clarify IP, change control, and quality agreements in writing.

What risks should I manage when working with a China CDMO?

Confirm regulatory documents are current and scoped to your product, validate reproducibility across batch scales, and establish clear communication and project governance.

Can a China CDMO deliver compliant, cost-effective inhalation devices?

China's inhalation-device manufacturing has matured significantly. With disciplined due diligence, a China CDMO can be a strong, compliant partner for bringing an inhalation product to market cost-effectively. This overview is for general reference; always verify a manufacturer's current regulatory status with the relevant authorities for your market and product.

Which inhalation platforms should a CDMO partner be able to provide?

A capable CDMO partner should provide multiple platforms, typically SMI, DPI, pMDI, and mesh nebulizer, allowing you to match the formulation to the right delivery platform under one partner.

Why consider a China-based CDMO for respiratory drug development?

Global respiratory drug developers partner with China-based CDMOs to accelerate development and reduce cost without sacrificing quality, provided due diligence is done properly.

Manufacturer note: Changzhou DSB Medical Co., Ltd. (China) offers inhalation device manufacturing with SMI, DPI, pMDI, and mesh nebulizer platforms under FDA, CE MDR, and ISO 13485 certified quality systems, with OEM/ODM CDMO services. Learn more: China medical device manufacturer — DSB Medical.
